text:
If your Saturday plans involve the waterfront, good news: this is exactly the day high pressure promised. It's already sunny and 81 with the humidity staying low, and the afternoon just holds that line, sunshine straight through to a high near 86. Winds stay south around 8 mph in town, though the lake itself is livelier, running 15 to 20 knots early and only easing to 10 to 15 later, with waves 1 to 3 feet, so it's a better afternoon for anyone who likes a bit of chop than for a flat-water paddle. Water's a swimmable 71, air quality's good, and skies stay mostly clear tonight with a comfortable low around 63.

Sunday holds the warmth, near 88, but the lake breeze cranks back up to 15 to 20 knots, so plan boat time accordingly. The real change is Monday, when the forecasters expect the pattern to break down into showers and thunderstorms, kicking off an unsettled week. Enjoy the dry stretch while it lasts, ideally on the water before evening, since after sunset around 8:26 the lake breeze won't be the only reason to head in.
